finding: §7.1 names one silent-failure hazard by name — "An empty guard list is a failed derivation, never a result" — and the registered check that is supposed to mechanize it can be defeated by the most likely edit the first task will make. Reproduced in a clean clone of the repo: (a) append `## The list` + `(the derivation produced nothing; filling in later)` to spec/0.34.0-guard-tests.md, leaving line 3 intact → exit 0, an empty guard list ships green; (b) append 100 copies of `internal/cli/nonexistent_test.go:TestTotallyMadeUp` and delete line 3 → exit 0, a wholly fabricated scope list ships green; (c) write the 100 entries as markdown bullets (`- path:TestX`, which still satisfies the documented "one file:function per line") → the LIST_ENTRY regex matches none of them and the count check is skipped entirely. Two independent weaknesses cause this. First, the body check is guarded by `elif PLACEHOLDER not in text`, and PLACEHOLDER is the sentence on line 3 of the file today ("Populated by the first task"); any edit that appends the list rather than rewriting the header — the natural edit — leaves that string in the file and permanently disables the check that property 3 of the script's own docstring exists to provide. Second, even when it does run, the check compares only the CARDINALITY of the entries against the derived count; `added_test_functions` already computes the exact set of (file, function) pairs and then discards the identities. So membership is never verified. This matters more than a stale number: §7.1 makes this list the scope of the entire §7 sweep, no reviewer will ever see it (it is produced during implementation, after review closes), and every reviewer is now told the class is mechanized and must not be reported — so the check is the sole line of defence over an artifact that decides which tests get deleted.

resolved.evidence: The list is compared as a set, not a count, so fabricated and duplicate entries fail; entries alongside the placeholder are a contradiction rather than an exemption; bullet-form entries are recognised. While the list is legitimately unwritten the check reports PENDING out loud, and section 7.1 now names the first task's acceptance as the observer that the check cannot be.

suggestion: Make the body check unconditional and make it compare sets, not sizes. (1) Delete the PLACEHOLDER exemption; instead treat "zero entries" as a failure always, and let the pre-task state satisfy it by an explicit, expiring marker the first task must remove (or simply accept that the check fails until the first task lands, which is the honest state). (2) Have `added_test_functions` return the `added` set it already builds, and compare it to the parsed entry set: report entries present in the document but absent from the derivation, and derived functions absent from the document. That closes the fabricated-list, duplicate-entry and wrong-window cases in one change. (3) Make the entry parser tolerate the formats the document's own wording permits (leading `- `, leading whitespace, backticks) or state the exact required line shape in the document so the parser and the prose cannot disagree.

finding: The check prints, on every run, `coverage: re-derivable counts only; estimates and historical observations are not covered and remain reportable`, and that sentence is what tells every reviewer to stop reporting the whole measured-claim class. The boundary it states is a boundary of claim KIND, but the check's real boundary is one of LOCATION: it inspects two sentence patterns in two files (spec/0.34.0.md and spec/0.34.0-guard-tests.md). Reproduced in a clone: appending `Note: this repository holds 42 test functions.` to CLAUDE.md → exit 0, while the identical sentence appended to spec/0.34.0.md is caught. The gap is not hypothetical for this release: §2.3 mandates that the release notes carry before-and-after counts for source lines, test count, exported symbols, documentation lines and multi-home facts — five re-derivable counts, every one of them inside the advertised coverage and none of them checked — and §5, §8.2, §8.3 and §9.3 each defer a count to "counted when the task runs". Reviewers suppressing the class on the strength of that coverage line will leave all of those unreviewed, which is worse than never having registered the check.

resolved.evidence: The coverage line states the boundary by location -- two claims in two named files -- rather than by claim kind, so it no longer reads as a promise over every number in the spec.

suggestion: State the coverage boundary by location as well as by kind, e.g. `coverage: re-derivable counts in spec/0.34.0.md and spec/0.34.0-guard-tests.md only; counts in CLAUDE.md, README.md, SKILL.md, REFERENCE.md and the release notes are NOT checked and remain reportable`. If §2.3's release-note counts are meant to be trustworthy, register their derivations too (each is a one-command count) rather than widening the claim without widening the check.

finding: §6.1 mandates action on test files that §7.4 fences off, and its only stated exemption ground does not cover the fence. §6.1 enables `dupl` "over production and test files alike" and requires that "every clone it reports is either merged or exempted", with the exemption ground named as the narrow one: "a clone whose merge would require a new abstraction is exempted, because Non-Goal 7 forbids inventing one." §7.4 protects "the equality tests introduced in §8, the config guard of §5, and any test whose failure would let a silent-write defect return" — but it fences "the sweep", which §7 defines as the test sweep only. So when `dupl` reports a clone between two protected tests (the §8.2 lint-rule equality test and the §8.3 flag-inventory equality test are described in near-identical terms and are the likeliest clone pair in this release), §6.1 requires them merged unless merging needs a new abstraction — and a straightforward table-driven merge needs none. The two sections then give opposite dispositions for the same file, and nothing in the spec says which wins. §7.4's own tie-breaker ("when in doubt the test stays") is scoped to §7 and does not reach a §6.1 task.
suggestion: Extend §6.1's exemption grounds by one clause so the fence crosses sweeps, e.g. "a clone whose merge would require a new abstraction is exempted, because Non-Goal 7 forbids inventing one, and so is a clone in a test §7.4 fences off" — or state in §7.4 that its fence binds every sweep in this release, not only §7's.

finding: Property 2 of the check's docstring claims "The derivation rule is READ FROM THE DOCUMENT, not held here", and cites the failure it fixed: "the numbers matched a rule nobody had asked for". Only the tag window is actually read from the document. The match rule — added-only, `^\+func Test`, `_test.go` files — remains hard-coded in the script, while §7.1 states that "The exact rule and the resulting count are that task's output, recorded in the file itself", i.e. the first task rewrites exactly the prose that is not pinned. Reproduced in a clone: rewording the document's rule to "Lines matching `^\+func (Test|Benchmark|Fuzz)` in any `.go` file, plus every modified test function" while leaving the command and the numbers untouched → exit 0. The document then records a rule that does not reproduce the numbers recorded beside it, and the check agrees with itself. The practical effect is inverted from the intent: because the numbers are pinned to the script's private rule, a task that legitimately adopts a different rule is forced to write numbers matching the script's rule, and its own prose is never checked.

resolved.evidence: The match rule is pinned from the document alongside the tag window, so rewording the rule while keeping the command and the numbers now fails.

suggestion: Either (a) pin the match rule the same way the window is pinned — extract the regex and the added-only/file-suffix conditions from the document (they are already written as literals in it) and drive the derivation from what was extracted, so a reworded rule changes the derivation rather than being ignored; or (b) drop property 2's claim to the general case and state in the docstring and in spec/0.34.0-guard-tests.md that only the tag window is read from the document and the match rule is fixed by the script, so a reviewer knows the rule prose is unguarded.

finding: `repo_test_functions` derives the repository total with `REPO.rglob("*_test.go")`, which walks the working tree including untracked and ignored files. Reproduced in a clone: dropping one untracked `scratch_notes_test.go` containing a single `func TestScratchOnly` into the repo root makes the check fail with `spec/0.34.0.md:177: states {'total': 1099}, derivation gives {'total': 1100}`. This release's own §7 sweep will be editing and moving test files, so a stray scratch file during a review round produces a failure whose obvious repair is to edit the number in the spec — committing a figure that only reproduces in the presence of untracked junk. The check is registered to run every review round, so it is exposed to the working tree, not to a commit.

resolved.evidence: The repository count derives from git ls-files, so an untracked scratch test file no longer fails the check and no longer teaches the wrong repair.

suggestion: Derive over tracked files only — `git ls-files '*_test.go'` (with `-z`) instead of `rglob` — so the count reproduces from any clean checkout of the same commit regardless of what else is sitting in the tree.
